Completion requires the twelve global acceptance tests in docs/roadmap/enterprise-oss-program.md plus file-level provenance and license compliance.

title: E1 Governance schemas and shared security invariants
description: Define tenant/principal/policy/key versions, control-plane RBAC versus data-plane entitlements, a single deny-by-default evaluator shared by model listing and inference, capability manifest, audit envelope, and cache-version contracts.

title: E2 Distributed virtual-key lifecycle
description: Harden existing OSS key CRUD with reveal-once hashed secrets, status/expiry/not-before, transactional rotation/revocation, versioned cross-pod invalidation, bounded stale-cache fail-closed behavior, audited bulk operations, and three-pod tests.

title: E3 Atomic hierarchical quotas and budgets
description: Implement shared atomic RPM/TPM/spend reservations and actual-usage reconciliation across global/BU/customer/team/user/profile/key/provider/model scopes, immediate audited top-ups, precise 429 responses, stuck-reservation repair, and partition semantics.

title: E4 OIDC, SCIM, Okta reconciliation, and entitlements
description: Implement OIDC Authorization Code with PKCE, standards-complete inbound SCIM Users/Groups, separate Okta directory importer, group-to-role/team/BU/access-profile mappings, lifecycle deprovisioning, managed-key issuance, and explain-access.

title: E5 Horizontal scaling and cluster operations
description: Make request pods stateless around durable config and shared counters; implement membership/invalidation, readiness/drain, migration locks, leader leases, HPA metrics, PDB/topology/network policy, rolling upgrades, and multi-zone failure tests.

title: E6 Adaptive routing, circuits, canaries, and shadows
description: Build the staged policy engine without bypassing entitlements; add health-weighted provider/key selection, circuit breakers, deterministic cohort canaries, separately budgeted side-effect-safe shadows, promotion gates, rollback, and decision explanations.

title: E7 Secure traces, replay, evaluation, and environment export
description: Emit OTEL/OpenInference-correlated trace envelopes with separated encrypted payloads; add side-effect-disabled replay, config snapshots, diffs/evaluators/promotion gates, and reviewed exports compatible with external RL/eval environment concepts.

title: E8 Honest enterprise operations dashboard
description: Replace or capability-hide stubs and cost cruft. Ship only API-backed Keys, Identity, Entitlements, Limits, Routing, Cluster, Traces/Replays, Audit, and reconciled-cost surfaces with RBAC, accessibility, and Playwright coverage.

title: E9 Threat model, audit integrity, and security verification
description: Threat-model tenant escape, stale auth, key theft, counter bypass, confused deputy, replay effects, SSRF and injection; add envelope encryption, redaction, tenant query scoping, tamper-evident audit, fuzz/race/chaos tests, and disclosure policy.

title: E10 Reproducible build, packaging, signing, and release
description: Adapt upstream workflows for the fork; emit cross-platform binaries, multi-arch OCI image, Helm chart, source archives, checksums, SBOM, license bundle, signatures and provenance; gate on tests, upgrades, scans, benchmarks, and asset verification.

title: E11 Agent flywheel and quality gates
description: Review the plan through strong-model rounds, polish beads to steady state, validate the DAG with br/bv robot modes, then use a small NTM swarm with one-bead claims and file reservations. Do not implement Wayfinder unless a concrete uncovered gap remains.

title: Prove RDS Proxy and direct PostgreSQL listener topology
description:
Build an executable oracle for Aurora PostgreSQL outbox wakeups across the launch listener topology: app traffic may use RDS Proxy/pooling, but durable outbox authority remains PostgreSQL and LISTEN/NOTIFY is only a wakeup hint.

Acceptance / failure oracles:
- A test harness runs one durable polling consumer plus the chosen listener path through Aurora writer failover and RDS Proxy interruption; every committed outbox row at or below the final watermark is applied exactly once or explicitly deduplicated by revision.
- The harness proves a direct listener reconnect gap cannot lose correctness because cursor polling catches all missed rows.
- The harness proves notifications delivered through an unsupported transaction-pooled path are not required for correctness and cannot be the only delivery mechanism.
- Duplicate, reordered, and missing notifications advance no local snapshot past the durable cursor and do not revive stale policy.
- Metrics expose listener reconnect count, poll catch-up lag, last applied revision, and stale-closed duration.

title: Prove optional Redis acceleration cannot become authority
description:
Define and test the optional Redis accelerator contract for horizontal scaling. Redis may reduce latency or fanout, but launch correctness must remain on Aurora/PostgreSQL authority, reservations, and outbox replay when Redis is absent or lost.

Acceptance / failure oracles:
- The same governance/config/MCP freshness suite passes with Redis disabled, Redis enabled, Redis flushed, Redis partitioned, and Redis restarted mid-stream.
- Redis loss never extends a revoked key, stale authorization epoch, exhausted reservation, disabled MCP grant, or reduced routing policy beyond the signed freshness lease.
- Redis-stored hints are either rebuilt from Aurora/outbox/bootstrap snapshots or ignored fail-closed; no Redis value is accepted without a durable revision/epoch check.
- Metrics distinguish accelerator hit/miss/loss from authoritative freshness and reservation decisions.
- Documentation names Redis as non-mandatory for Kubernetes launch and lists the exact features that may use it only as an accelerator.

title: Prove authority leases under clock skew
description:
Build deterministic tests for freshness leases, authorization epochs, outbox cursors, and reservation expiry under pod, node, and database clock skew. The oracle must prove launch behavior uses monotonic revisions and database/lease authority rather than trusting local pod wall clocks.

Acceptance / failure oracles:
- With pod clocks skewed forward and backward beyond the freshness lease, revoked keys, removed groups, reduced budgets, disabled MCP grants, and reduced routing policies fail stale-closed by logical revision/epoch and cannot be prolonged by local time.
- Reservation expiry and renewal tests use a single authoritative time source or fenced compare-and-swap state; stale renewals cannot revive abandoned reservations.
- Outbox application order remains revision/watermark based when event timestamps are equal, reversed, or skewed.
- Kubernetes readiness/startup refuses protected traffic before an initial signed snapshot regardless of local clock.
- Metrics expose clock-skew suspicion separately from ordinary outbox lag or DB outage.

title: Prove 100-pod bootstrap backpressure and notification storms
description:
Build the horizontal-scaling acceptance oracle that goes beyond the three-pod conformance suite: 100 stateless pods cold-start, catch up from Aurora/PostgreSQL authority, and survive notification storms without making Redis mandatory.

Acceptance / failure oracles:
- A 100-pod test boots from empty local state against a bounded Aurora/outbox backlog; pods do not accept protected requests until an initial signed snapshot and required cursors are installed.
- Notification storms, reordered wakeups, and dropped wakeups cannot create duplicate application, cursor regression, stale policy revival, or DB thundering herd beyond configured backpressure limits.
- Backpressure protects Aurora by bounding concurrent bootstrap readers, LISTEN reconnects, snapshot downloads, and per-tenant catch-up work while preserving starvation-free progress.
- Pod, node, and zone loss during bootstrap/recovery leaves surviving pods available within the documented stale-closed rules and lets replacement pods converge from durable state.
- The report records actual lag, queue depth, retry, WAL/autovacuum, and CPU/memory data without inventing benchmark thresholds before measurement.
